text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Danish ports have charged illegal port taxes from other European Union ships from 1984 to 1990, an interim judgement from the European Court in Luxembourg says.
--- Last year's mad cow disease in Britain encouraged Danish consumers to switch to pork products, pushing pork producers' hourly wage from 119 crowns in 1995 to 175 crowns in 1996.

--- Shipping group A.P. Moeller's container ship unit Maersk Line could profit from discussions between the U.S.A. and Japan on free access to Japanese ports. At present loading and unloading at Japanese ports costs large container ship companies several million crowns a year.
--- Increasing imports of generic medicines are pressing prices down and have already given taxpayers savings of 200 million crowns on reduced prescription subsidies, importers say.
